about: #220 / ADR-0014 decision 6, amended by #231 — the hand-labeled measurement grid the job labeler must pass before it is trusted, and the permanent regression harness for every later prompt change. Drafted by the agent, arbitrated by the owner (see arbitration:true cases). Real model calls: run it deliberately (pnpm --filter @jobcrush/api eval:labeler), never in fast-lane CI.

vocabularies.published: The real closed vocabulary as published today, read live off the registry (harness.ts): it-project-delivery + business-analysis at v2, product-management at v1 (#361). Publishing a family silently changes what every stranger case is asked — re-run the grid and re-arbitrate affected strangers as part of publishing (#263's lesson).

expectations.confirmed: expectedFamilies must match as a SET — a confirmation into the wrong family, or one that names a spurious second family, is a miss, not partial credit.
expectations.unmapped: the honest no-family answer. A near-miss role landing here is the labeler working, not failing.
expectations.expectedConfidence: asserted only where the right ordinal is not in doubt, and REPORTED rather than barred: the families are the gate. A labeler one step out on an ordinal is worth seeing, not worth failing a run over.
expectations.dual-family: #231 — the cases that measure amendment 1 decision 1. A second family is named only when BOTH parts of the work are substantial; the amb-01/02/06/07 cases are the control group, where 'product' is the SUBJECT of delivery work rather than a second craft, and a second family there is a miss.

OWNER ARBITRATED 2026-08-21 (#263): OUT. The replacement near-miss for str-13, which moved IN when business-analysis published — shares two of three words with the family's own label, and is the sharpest stranger for it. Tested, not argued: of #260's floor corpus narrowed to the 7 purely-BI adverts, 0 ask for requirements elicitation, 0 for spec writing, 7% for workshops, 7% for UAT — against 48-65% across the 80 Business Analyst adverts. A business analyst works with people to decide what should change; a BI analyst works with data to describe what happened. Was RED 2026-08-21 (the labeler confirmed it into business-analysis, twice measured). #265's first fix — a near-is-not-in prompt paragraph alone — looked green on two runs but was caught by QA as a coin flip: 3 green / 2 red across five runs. The fix that held adds a product discriminator (name what the role PRODUCES, check the scope claims it) and moves the output's why BEFORE the outcome so the check runs before the answer token: green 5 of 5 consecutive runs 2026-08-23, stranger recall 100% and false-unknown 0% on every one. This case is flip-prone by nature — on any future red, re-run several times before calling it noise. Self-resolves further the day a data/business-intelligence family publishes (see candidate-families.md). 'Systems Analyst' stays deliberately absent: #260's corpus classified a Systems Analyst advert in-family while #265 lists the title as out — an open edge question, not grid material.
